forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Wheat is already surging at $247. With extreme European heat (+2.11°C) and thin stockpiles, markets grossly underestimate how quickly a supply squeeze will push prices past $272.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Sovereign forward contracts are draining open-market milling wheat. With El Niño and European warmth, minor supply shocks trigger outsized rallies beyond current depressed pricing.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Escalating Black Sea attacks and war-risk freight spikes create a fat right tail. Chokepoint fragility makes a surge past $272 far more plausible than priced.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Broad ag reflation lifts the grain complex, and fund flows follow dollar trends; market underprices the momentum across grains heading into early 2027.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Black Sea escalation and high input costs limit supply growth, but global output cushions spikes. Weather and regulatory burdens still support prices above market pricing.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Climate shocks and regional instability drive yield volatility; degraded Mediterranean soils and extreme weather make price spikes more frequent than markets assume.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Black Sea escalation presents upside geopolitical risk to grain logistics, though elevated foreign farmgate supports temper medium-term import demand.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Black Sea logistics frictions elevate Mediterranean import costs, though trade rerouting and foreign farmer price incentives moderate long-term price spikes.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Ample Russian export flows and global stock cushions limit upside, though Black Sea transit flare-ups sustain a background risk premium.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Durum sits dormant through winter. While pre-harvest tightening aids March prices, plentiful Mediterranean and Black Sea supplies limit a +10% surge past $272.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Ample global cereal acreage and resilient EU production cap upside, despite Black Sea shipping frictions.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Balance sheets reflect solid export competition from Russia and higher regional support prices, keeping upside capped unless major supply deficits emerge.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Market prices this low at 14%. Wheat has upward momentum recently, so I lean slightly higher while sticking close to consensus.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: High prices call forth supply. With global production adapting and markets flattening post-spike, a sustained rally above $272 is unlikely.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Wheat's run from $155 to $247 has stretched valuations. High prices induce supply and curb demand; pushing further past $272 fades against historical mean reversion.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: High grain prices trigger strong global acreage expansions and technological adaptation, capping upside well before $272/mt.
